Security model

Is XERJ safe to run? Closed by default.

A node you have not configured listens on 127.0.0.1 only and demands an API key on every request. Exposing it to a network needs TLS or an explicit opt-out, the installer refuses a binary whose SHA-256 does not match, and xerj ask refuses any catalogue or corpus pack that fails its ed25519 signature. --insecure turns TLS and auth off, for one user on one machine. This page lists what each default does, what leaves your machine, and how to report a vulnerability.

Defaults

What a fresh node does

Bindbind_address defaults to 127.0.0.1: reachable from its own host and nowhere else. Set --bind or XERJ_BIND_ADDRESS to expose it.
Plain HTTP on a networkWith TLS off, a non-loopback bind refuses to start, because the API key would cross the wire in cleartext. Enable [tls] with PEM cert and key, or declare server.allow_insecure_network_bind = true when a proxy in front already terminates TLS. --insecure trips the same check.
AuthOn by default. The first start writes a 64-character hex admin key to <data_dir>/admin.key with mode 0600; the banner names the file and does not print the key. Clients send Authorization: ApiKey <key>. Rotation is delete the file and restart.
CORSOff: no Access-Control-* headers unless [cors] allowed_origins lists an origin.
--insecureDisables TLS and API-key auth. Local development only.
MCP serverxerj mcp runs over stdio and starts no listener. For a loopback node with no XERJ_AUTH set, it reads admin.key itself and says which file it used; it never does that for a non-loopback URL.

Configuration details: Auth & TLS · Config TOML.

Supply chain

Verified bytes, or nothing

  • Installer. xerj.org/get downloads the release from GitHub and verifies its SHA-256 before installing. A missing or mismatched checksum aborts; if no hashing tool exists (it tries sha256sum, shasum, openssl, sha256, busybox, cksum) it refuses to install. Skipping the check is opt-in only, with XERJ_INSECURE_SKIP_CHECKSUM=1. Every release asset has a .sha256 next to it.
  • Corpus packs. The binary embeds the hub's ed25519 public key. The catalogue and every pack must pass the signature and SHA-256 checks before anything is extracted; a tampered one is refused (exit 3). A build with no key downloads nothing (exit 5).
  • Pull limits. xerj ask pulls on its own only packs of 50 MB or less and never a pack whose licence class is Excluded.

Data

What leaves your machine

  • Indexing and search: nothing. xerj autoindex, xerj search and the HTTP API work against your local node. The default embedder is lexical and runs in-process; a neural model is downloaded only with --embed-mode neural.
  • xerj ask: the pack download, and maybe the question. Routing runs in the client. With the default --hosted auto, a question asked outside a git repository may be sent to the hosted hub API; inside a repository it is not. xerj hub config hosted off keeps every question local. The hub's privacy section lists what it logs: no cookies or user id, records deleted after 40 days, totals only, and DNT or Sec-GPC honoured (hub.xerj.org/about).
  • Field reports: only when sent. The CLI and docs ask agents to send a short report after use; it goes to a GitHub pull request, or to xerj.org/api/field-report when GitHub is unavailable. --disable-feedback or XERJ_DISABLE_FEEDBACK=true opts out. Keep secrets out of it.

Not in the binary

What XERJ does not do

  • Roles are not enforced. GET /_security/roles lists stored roles and says so itself: every authenticated caller has full access. Treat the API key as an admin credential.
  • No single sign-on. No user management, LDAP, SAML or OIDC.
  • No encryption-at-rest option is documented. Put the data directory on an encrypted disk.
  • No audit certifications. The project documents no SOC 2, ISO 27001 or similar audit.

Disclosure

Report a vulnerability

Do not open a public issue. Email security@xerj.org or use GitHub's private vulnerability reporting on xerj-org/xerj. The security policy commits to acknowledging within 72 hours and an initial assessment typically within 7 days, with coordinated disclosure. Fixes go to the latest 1.0.0-rc line.
